main_version.subject: Overnight volume watch: data-only BOATS significant-volume monitor over the full overnight-tradable universe (#480)
main_version.pr_head_subject: Overnight volume watch: repair round for the GPT-6 review of #480
main_version.thresholds_and_monitor_py: unchanged: the same sha256 at the run commit, at 1b8d63349e5c and at the base f03f41c7
differences_that_matter_here: push records: the run's code writes one push record per attempt, after the POST, carrying status sent or failed; main writes a push record fsynced before the POST and a push_result record after it. The run's alerts.jsonl therefore has push records with status and no push_result records.
rate-limit probe: in the run's code a failed or rate-limited first chunk did not stop the sweep's fan-out; main stops it. No chunk failed in this run.
plan: the run's plan counts the first minute as the daily-bar passes plus the average sweep rate (108); main counts both passes plus a whole first sweep (118). Both stay under the 500 cap.
start-up: main checks a stop request and a 600 s deadline before every start-up request and refuses an --out inside a git worktree; the run's code does neither.
main_version.source: git diff dca569ae 1b8d63349e5c -- watch.py and the PR head commit message (repair round for the GPT-6 review of #480)

settings.plan_note: Written by the watch at start. data_cap_per_min is 5% of the data API's 10,000 per minute; the plan broke no rule (refusals empty).

startup.note: The start-up made exactly the planned 99 calls (1 asset list and 2 daily-bar passes of 49 requests). Every attempt is a counted call, so no start-up request was retried and none needed a second page.

roll_probe.note: SPY's BOATS dailyBar.t stayed at the trade date in every sweep, across midnight ET, and no session_bar_rolled record was written. This observes directly what the overnight-volume README lists as inferred: the BOATS daily bar is keyed to the session and does not roll at ET midnight.

calls.failed_requests_basis: all 3,520 snapshot chunks returned ok (a failed chunk is recorded with status error and its message), and the start-up made exactly its planned calls

busiest_minute.note: A 60 s window holds at most one sweep start at the 120 s cadence, so every minute has at most 20 calls except the one that can hold the start-up's 99 calls and the first sweep's 20.

errors.http_429_basis: None. A snapshot chunk that failed, a 429 included, is recorded with status error and its message; all 3,520 returned ok. The start-up retries are not written per attempt, but every attempt is a counted call and the start-up made exactly its 99 planned calls. The lowest remaining data allowance was 9,998 of 10,000.

basis: Code: watch.py sends every Alpaca request through GuardedHttp.get, which checks an allow-list of three GET endpoints (paper trading /v2/assets, data /v2/stocks/snapshots and /v2/stocks/bars) before monitor.Http.get makes the request. The only other request is the notify POST to the loopback ntfy URL that check_notify_url validates.
Recorded calls: 1 asset list, 98 daily-bar requests and 3,520 snapshot requests, all allow-listed GETs, plus 6 posts to the loopback ntfy topic.
Broker listing: none. No broker read covers 02:09Z-08:00Z on 2026-09-29 for account 1, so the statement rests on the code and the recorded calls.

units.note: Launched from an interactive shell, not from a systemd unit (the coordinator's brief); systemctl --user list-unit-files lists no overnight-volume unit on 2026-09-30. There is no unit journal, and the process's console output was not retained.

limitations: Data-only watch: it evaluates no strategy and qualifies no gate. The tiers are unvalidated monitoring thresholds.
BOATS is one ATS, so its volume is indicative venue data, not consolidated volume. The fund tag misses some ETFs.

The code is not on main: the run commit dca569ae is in no local ref (remote-tracking branches included) and not in the history of refs/pull/480/head. Its watch.py is the same blob as 6545d7ad in that history, and main's version differs (code.main_version).
No systemd unit: there is no unit journal, and the process's console output was not retained. The key pair (account 1) is not recorded in the run's files.
No broker read covers the watch window on account 1; the no-order statement rests on the code and the recorded calls.
Posts are recorded as sent when the POST returned without an error; delivery was not checked.
The first sweep came 130.0 minutes after the session opened at 20:00 ET. The session bar's volume is cumulative, so the first sweep's alerts include activity from before the watch started.
14 of the 9,683 watched names never returned a snapshot.
